acceptance.condition: A new correction-integration helper/operator surface accepts only an exact TASK/revision + cumulative-tip RUN/SHA + current-main SHA authorization and derives one content-addressed integration identity with idempotent exact replay and fail-closed collision/staleness behavior.

For a clean divergence, integration creates exactly one dedicated candidate merge commit/ref whose parents are exactly [cumulative tip candidate, authorized main], whose tree equals the clean deterministic Git merge result, and which leaves the persistent worktree, branch, main ref, RUN namespace, and Executor invocation count unchanged.
Any merge conflict or inability to prove the exact clean merge fails closed before an integration ref/candidate becomes authoritative and does not invoke an Executor or mutate main.

Prospective REMEDIATION can persist and consume a backward-compatible integrated execution-base form that keeps the semantic predecessor and canonical cumulative tip distinct while setting Run.base_sha to the exact integration candidate.

Correction Preflight, Unified State, and actual execution agree: the observed TASK-133-shaped divergence is INTEGRATION_REQUIRED before the exact integration exists and becomes remediation-ready from the same integrated base afterward; any later main/tip movement invalidates that base.

Integrated remediation completion measures Executor mutation and scope from the integration candidate, so unrelated main-only content already merged into the base is not reported as remediation changed_files.

Publication independently proves the integrated base, cumulative RUN/RESULT, authorized main parent, integration ref, merge tree, and final ancestry before any main fast-forward; forged/moved/stale integration state remains rejected.

Existing v1/non-integrated cumulative remediation, A3 approval, A6 dispatch, Reviewer, Publisher, Runtime verification, correction frontier, historical artifacts, and frozen Kernel behavior remain compatible; integration introduces no generic merge authority, retry, reroute, fallback, or new lifecycle family.
Focused deterministic tests pass, git diff checking passes, RESULT contains zero unresolved items, and production mutation stays within the explicitly authorized files.

assumptions: TASK-133 RUN-133-001 is a canonical RESULT whose result.head_sha is e1f0f4106b5e6f7c80fc1d1354ce730f432f8ae4; its semantic REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage remains immutable and must not be rewritten.

The observed divergence is conflict-free in content because current main advanced only by adding .ai/tasks/TASK-134.yaml, but the implementation must be generic and must not special-case TASK-133, TASK-134, filenames, or this exact SHA pair.

TASK-099 revision 2 and TASK-103 revision 2 remain authoritative: current main must be contained by the actual prospective execution base; divergence fails closed; Runtime must not auto-merge, auto-rebase, replay, or select integration.

Frozen Kernel v0.1 remains frozen. Human owns integration authorization, Brain may frame the exact bounded integration intent, Runtime owns deterministic validation/materialization, Executor owns implementation only after normal REMEDIATION admission, and Reviewer/Publisher retain their existing authorities.

hard: Integration is explicit. The operator command must require an exact bounded authorization binding containing TASK id/revision, cumulative tip RUN id, cumulative tip candidate SHA, and expected current-main SHA. The operation must reject stale or mismatched selectors before creating any integration candidate.
Derive a deterministic integration identity from the exact authorization binding. Repeating the same binding is idempotent; reusing an integration identity with any changed binding fails closed.

The integration operation must not invoke codex, antigravity, MiniMax, another coding model, canonical verification, Reviewer, or Publisher. It is deterministic Git integration under explicit Human authorization, not implementation work.

Materialize integration outside the normal product worktree using bounded Git plumbing or an isolated temporary workspace. The persistent checkout must remain clean and on its original branch/HEAD throughout success and failure.

Version 1 supports conflict-free integration only. The exact integration tree must equal Git's clean merge result for the authorized cumulative-tip candidate and current-main commit. Any conflict, ambiguous merge-base condition, missing object, dirty/untrusted state, or inability to prove the exact merge tree fails closed without an integration ref.

A successful integration candidate must be a merge commit whose first parent is the exact cumulative-tip candidate and whose second parent is the exact authorized current-main SHA, so the resulting candidate is provably descended from both. The operation may create/push only its dedicated content-addressed refs/heads/aios/integration/<integration_id> ref and must never move main.

Prospective REMEDIATION execution-base grammar must gain a backward-compatible integrated form while preserving the existing legacy/cumulative form. The integrated form must bind at least: version/kind, cumulative tip RUN id, cumulative tip candidate SHA, authorized main SHA, integration candidate SHA, and integration identity. Run.base_sha must equal the actual integration candidate SHA.

Existing execution-base semantics remain exact: semantic predecessor identity is unchanged; the canonical cumulative tip RUN/RESULT remains separately provable; the integration candidate must never masquerade as that RUN's RESULT candidate.

Remediation admission may consume an integration candidate only when the exact deterministic integration ref exists and validates against the current canonical lifecycle, current main, exact cumulative tip, exact parents, and clean merge tree. If main or the cumulative tip changes after integration, the old candidate is stale and admission returns INTEGRATION_REQUIRED again.

Correction Preflight and Unified State must agree with execution. Before a valid integration candidate exists they continue to fail closed with INTEGRATION_REQUIRED; after the exact candidate exists they report/consume the same integrated execution base without creating a RUN or invoking an Executor.

For integrated REMEDIATION, code delta, Result.changed_files, modification-scope enforcement, and affected verification are measured from the actual integrated Run.base_sha. Unrelated current-main content already present in the integration base must not be misclassified as Executor mutation.

Publication must independently validate the integrated execution base from remote evidence: exact integration ref, exact cumulative RUN/RESULT candidate, exact authorized main SHA, exact merge parents, clean deterministic merge tree, and final reviewed candidate ancestry. It must reject fabricated, moved, stale, conflicting, or semantically unprovable integration bases.
Existing non-integrated REMEDIATION RUNs remain byte/behavior compatible under the established execution-base contract. No historical backfill or reinterpretation is allowed.

Integration state/ref is operational staging authority only. It cannot claim TASK completion, verification, review acceptance, publication safety, or roadmap completion and cannot alter correction-frontier meaning.

A prior pre-RUN A6 delivery that failed on INTEGRATION_REQUIRED remains immutable at-most-once history. After successful integration, execution requires a fresh correction_dispatch_id bound to the same still-current Human approval; no hidden retry/replay of the rejected delivery is permitted.

Deterministic offline regressions must cover exact binding, idempotent replay, stale-main rejection, stale-tip rejection, conflict rejection with zero ref, clean two-parent integration, worktree non-mutation, integrated preflight/state readiness, actual remediation base binding, changed-file baseline correctness, publication validation, v1 compatibility, and no Executor invocation by integration.

task.goal: Close the explicit INTEGRATION_REQUIRED recovery gap for prospective cumulative REMEDIATION by adding one separately authorized, deterministic, conflict-free correction-integration base. The integration base must preserve the immutable semantic predecessor and canonical correction tip, contain the exact current main, introduce no semantic implementation edits of its own, and become the actual REMEDIATION Run.base_sha only after exact fail-closed validation.
non_goals: Automatically integrate whenever INTEGRATION_REQUIRED is observed, or let Runtime, Unified State, Correction Preflight, A6, a workflow, or an Executor silently choose merge/rebase/cherry-pick behavior.

Resolve merge conflicts, semantic conflicts, or code conflicts. Any non-clean deterministic merge must fail closed for fresh Brain/Human intent rather than invoking a coding Executor to guess a resolution.
Move, reset, force-update, rewrite, or publish canonical main as part of the integration operation.
Rewrite RUN-133-001, REVIEW-133-001, its RESULT/EVIDENCE, remediation approval, correction-dispatch history, or any historical TASK-133 lineage.
Reuse a correction_dispatch_id whose earlier A6 invocation already failed before RUN creation; existing A6 at-most-once and reconciliation semantics remain unchanged.
Add a generic merge service, planner, lifecycle router, queue, scheduler, retry, reroute, fallback, model selection, background worker, or autonomous correction loop.
Add a new semantic RUN family or treat an integration candidate as RESULT, EVIDENCE, REVIEW, REMEDIATION, REPAIR, or publication truth.

Add remote GitHub Issue/workflow convenience for integration in this task. A reviewed local/operator primitive is sufficient; remote carrier work, if desired, is a separate follow-up after the core invariant is proven.
Do not push or publish from coding Executor implementation execution.
task.problem: TASK-133 RUN-133-001 produced canonical RESULT candidate e1f0f4106b5e6f7c80fc1d1354ce730f432f8ae4 and REVIEW-133-001 reported FINDING-133-001. The approved remediation is canonically bound at 4820915790f424286b616fd8a26fd64891c5f674. Before that remediation executed, canonical main advanced from the shared base b05f00a96720ade9b6c540a987bfcd356af6067b to 617e85a77503951d1b82d574c7839e415d84b05d solely by authoring TASK-134. Cumulative remediation admission correctly fails closed because current main is not an ancestor of the RUN-133-001 candidate. TASK-099/TASK-103 intentionally prohibit automatic merge/rebase and require separately authorized integration, but AIOS has no bounded integration primitive. Merely merging the correction branch into main cannot repair the admission direction because the immutable cumulative tip would still not contain the newer main. AIOS therefore needs a narrow operational integration base that contains both exact parents and can be proven independently before REMEDIATION execution.
